title: Senior Data Platform — 30/60/90 Ramp + Interview Heuristics (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working kit for hiring and ramping a Senior Data Platform engineer (IC4). Combines interview heuristics, a lightweight scorecard, and an accelerated 30/60/90 onboarding checklist tailored to our platform cadence. Designed to be used by hiring managers, interviewers, and hiring ops during fast-moving cycles.

Status note to reviewers: rough — lots of bullets, open questions marked with TODO. Use as a source-of-truth for candidate selection and immediate post-offer ramp plan.

Role snapshot (target persona):
- Senior Platform engineer with strong infra + data pipeline experience (Kafka, Flink/Spark, k8s operators)
- Comfortable owning cross-team integrations and SLOs for data quality
- History of mentoring + shaping system design with pragmatic tradeoffs
- Prefer candidates who have shipped cost-conscious streaming or batch infra at scale

Hiring plan summary (high level):
- Timeline: 4-week sourcing -> 2-week interview loop -> offer week -> 2-week notice typical
- Interview loop: Recruit screen (30m) -> Technical screen (coding + infra) (60m) -> System design + troubleshooting (90m) -> Onsite/virtual loop with 3 interviews (design, coding/ops, cross-team behavioral) -> Hiring manager debrief
- Decision owners: Hiring manager (final), tech lead (technical read), People ops (offer/package)

Scorecard heuristic (use numeric 1-5; 5 = outstanding):
- System design: scalability, data correctness, tradeoffs (weight 30%)
- Operational excellence: debugging at scale, SLOs, observability (weight 25%)
- Core infra knowledge: stream/batch engines, k8s, storage (weight 20%)
- Collaboration & leadership: async comms, mentoring, cross-team influence (weight 15%)
- Product sense: understands customer cost/latency constraints (weight 10%)

Thresholds (guidance):
- Strong hire: weighted avg >= 4.2 and no score < 3 in ops or design
- Hire with reservation: avg 3.7-4.2 and clear development plan or senior exec sponsorship
- No hire: avg < 3.5 or critical blind spots in ops/design

Interview heuristics and example prompts:
1) Recruiter screen (30m)
- Goal: verify background fit, compensation alignment, open visa/relocation constraints, and curiosity about our product.
- Script snippet: "Tell me about a pipeline you owned end-to-end — what went wrong, what you changed, what you measure now?"

2) Technical screen (60m) — live code + ops question
- 30m coding micro-problem (Python/Go): small algo or data transformation. Emphasize clarity and testability, not trick questions. Example: stream deduplication sketch, efficient windowing outline.
- 30m ops question: given a spike causing delayed ingestion, talk through triage. Look for hypothesis-driven approach, use of metrics, rollback plan, and RCA discipline.

3) System design (90m)
- Give candidate a real problem: "Design a multi-tenant streaming ETL that supports exactly-once semantics for downstream OLAP tables with backpressure handling and replay. Assume 10k events/sec and bursty traffic."
- Look for: architecture diagrams, state management, checkpointing/offset management, cost tradeoffs, testing strategy, migration/rollout approach.
- Red flags: hand-wavy answers on failure modes, no metrics to validate correctness, inability to break big problems into milestones.

4) Behavior / cross-team interview (60m)
- Topics: conflict with product owners, mentoring junior engineers, examples of driving infra improvements with limited bandwidth.
- Probe: "Describe a time you pushed back on a feature for operational reasons — how did you persuade stakeholders?"

Interviewer guidance (quick bullets):
- Start with a 2–3 min context statement; tell candidate the role of the interviewer in the process.
- Use STAR for behavioral questions but accept shorter answers if timeboxed.
- Rate to rubric after the interview and write 2–3 concrete evidence bullets for each criteria. Do not use only gut feel.

Onboarding 30/60/90 — accelerated plan (post-offer):
- Before day 1 (week 0): set up seat (laptop image), dev VPN, k8s access, Cloud Console roles, list of must-read docs (arch diagram, SLO runbook), assign buddy.

First 30 days (orientation + core context):
- Goals: gain system-level context, runbook familiarity, merge small infra fix
- Week 1: meet core team, pair on dev environment, complete local end-to-end pipeline run, shadow on-call for 1 rotation (read-only)
- Week 2: implement one small oncall automation (e.g., alert tuning PR), document findings, complete two onboarding quizzes (arch + deployment flow)
- Week 3: own a small bugfix from triage to prod with mentor sign-off
- Week 4: present "platform walkthru" to team (15m) and submit a 30d blameless retrospective note

30–60 days (ownership ramp):
- Goals: own a non-trivial component, solidify cross-team relationships, propose one measurable improvement
- Deliverables: lead a rollout for a small config change, create a runbook improvement PR, mentor a junior for a shadow task

60–90 days (impact + scale):
- Goals: deploy measurable improvement, take on pager rotations, propose roadmap item aligned with product needs
- Deliverables: run a canary rollout, quantify cost/latency baseline and improvement, run a post-change retro

First-week checklist (practical):
- Hardware & accounts verified (IT ticket #)
- Access to code repos and infra dashboards
- PagerDuty linked and test notification confirmed
- Buddy assigned and intro meetings scheduled
- First-oncall shadow scheduled

Knowledge transfer and docs to create (expected in first 60 days):
- README: local dev + replay instructions (short, copyable commands)
- Runbook: major incident checklist and key dashboards
- Migration plan template for any schema changes

Risk flags (screening & early-onboarding):
- Candidate: dismisses observability or testing, cannot articulate basic failure modes
- Early onboard: misses basic access for >5 workdays, fails to follow up on assigned small PRs, avoids oncall shadowing

Notes to hiring managers / interviewers:
- If candidate has strong design but shallow ops, consider "hire and craft" with explicit 6-month oncall mentorship and measurable milestones.
- For remote hires, emphasize async comms examples during loop.
- Keep compensation calibrated with internal comp bands; get People Ops early on pricing for fast decisions.

Open TODOs / questions:
- Decide whether to require a short home assignment for senior infra candidates (pros: signal; cons: slows loop). TODO: discuss with hiring manager and pipeline velocity metrics (ask recruiting).
- Agree on standard set of "must-read" docs to share pre-day-1 (arch diagram location) — TODO: platform documentation owner to confirm link.

Appendix: Sample interviewer evidence bullets (copy into debrief):
- System design: candidate proposed layered architecture with idempotent sinks + checkpointing; listed three failure scenarios and remediation steps.
- Ops: used metrics-driven triage, suggested a fast rollback path and a safer progressive rollout.
- Collaboration: clearly documented decisions in proposal, suggested pairing plan for rollout.

Logistics / next steps:
- Share this doc with recruiting team and platform hiring panel.
- Collect feedback after first two loops and iterate rubric scores.
- Move to finalized onboarding checklist after 3 hires validate content.

Notes to self (Maya):

- Check recruiting velocity for "home assignment" decision by 2025-03-12.

End of doc.
